title: Lily Hop
tags: adding,addition,subtraction,take away,number partners,number bonds,make ten,number line,add to 20,kindergarten,first grade,math,maths,3d,pond,frogs,read aloud,learning
description: Hop across a sunny 3D pond! Count frogs as they hop together, find the number partner that is missing, and hop along a row of numbered lily pads to add and take away up to 20. Every instruction is read aloud, so you can play before you can read.
notes: Number Quest Launchpad Unit 2, The Joining Pond (kindergarten to grade 1): a Kit 2 game on Oomba3D 1.1.0 in the Sky Islands theme 1.0.1 (daytime, ink outlines, gear button, graphics 'auto'), loaded with exactly kit2ImportMap() (tests/unit/lily-hop.test.js checks the literal map). The sea is the library's own (world.water), its swell turned down to pond ripples through the returned object, with a blue floor under it; every lily pad and island is the theme's round island, and the frogs, trees, hut and lighthouse are the game's own simple meshes. Made for a child who cannot read: every instruction is short, shown and spoken through BRB.speak (voice role friendly; the speaker button says it again), numbers are big, and every round is answered by tapping one of three number pads in the pond or the matching big button; the helper hops there. No timer, no lives, no fail state: a wrong pad dips and wobbles (a dashed outline on the button with reduced motion), the helper hops back and gives a spoken hint, then another try. Three chapters of six rounds, made by window.LilyHop.round(chapter, n, lap) (the block between /* lily-hop:begin */ and /* lily-hop:end */, pure, seeded from the round number; a replay lap gets new numbers): join (step 2.1; K.OA.A.1, K.OA.A.2): rounds 1-4 two groups of frogs on two pads, how many in all (totals 2-4, 4-6, 6-8, 8-10), shown and said as '3 and 2 make 5'; rounds 5-6 some frogs hop away, how many are left (from 4-6, then 7-10). apart (2.2; K.OA.A.3, K.OA.A.4): rounds 1-2 split the same number (4-6) two different ways, round 3 a bigger one (7-9), '5 is 2 and what?'; rounds 4-6 a ten-frame of spots, '7 and what make 10?' (7-9, then 4-6, then 1-3). twenty (2.3; 1.OA.C.6, also 1.OA.B.3): a row of numbered pads with a flag on 10: 1 ten and some more, 2 add over ten, 3 round 2 turned round (the same answer, said as '5 and 8 is the same as 8 and 5'), 4 take away inside the teens, 5 take away back over ten, 6 add over ten again; over ten the helper stops on 10 and the sum is shown and said in two steps (8 + 2 = 10, 3 more makes 13). A wide screen shows as many pads as fit at tap size (all of 0-20 from about 1250 px); a phone shows the pads the round hops over. The player picks one of the theme's five adventurers as a helper. Lesson mode: BRB.params { chapter: join | apart | twenty, lock: 1 } opens that chapter only; finishing its six rounds calls BRB.gameOver({ won: true }) once (the single call site), which completes the course step. With no parameters a picture menu offers the three chapters. Save: BRB.storage 'lily-hop-v1' holds only which chapters are finished. Layout: wide screens set the frog pads side by side, tall phones one behind the other; the camera looks across the pond so the islands show behind the play area, and backs off until the play area fits between the words and the buttons. Keyboard: every answer is a button (Tab, Enter, Space). A device without WebGL2 or import maps gets the site's 'needs a newer device' card (the SDK's check for import-map games). Words: English only (the I18N block, read by server/services/tts-lines.js for AI voices). Test handle: window.__lh (also window.__brbTest): state(), fast(), hero(id), act('answer', n), spot(n), heroAt().
